chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abi al-Abbas, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife after she had given birth and purified herself, and she is a woman who does not see blood for as long as she breastfeeds. What is her waiting period? He (peace be upon him) said: Three months.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a breastfeeding woman with irregular menstruation who is divorced?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific ruling for a nursing mother who is divorced after her postpartum bleeding has ceased and she does not experience regular menstruation, establishing her iddah as three months. This ruling aligns with the general principle for women with irregular menstruation (harrah) and highlights the practical application of Quranic verses in distinguishing between postpartum purity and menstrual cycles within Shia jurisprudence. It serves as a key precedent for determining the waiting period when the primary indicator of menstruation is absent due to nursing.
